# BASIC FIRST AID UNTIL HELP ARRIVES [italic]What to do in the minutes before the medic gets there. None of it replaces the clinic.[/italic]
## FIRST, ALWAYS - Make sure the danger is over before you go in. Two patients are worse than one. - Call for the clinic by radio, intercom or by sending the fastest runner you have. - Stay with the patient. Talk to them. Tell them help is coming, because it is.
## BLEEDING Press a gauze pad hard on the wound and keep pressing. Do not lift it to look. If the patient can take tablets, a red bottle tablet helps. A patient who has lost a lot of blood needs the clinic, not the counter.
## BURNS Cool the burn with clean water for as long as you can spare. Then cover it with burn ointment and a loose dressing. A yellow bottle tablet helps. Do not burst blisters. Do not use galley grease. Somebody always tries.
## BAD AIR AND SMOKE Get the patient into clean air first, even before you get them into a bed. Then a blue bottle tablet. If the air is bad where they are, it is bad for you too. Put your mask on before you go in.
## POISONING AND TOXINS A green bottle tablet, and tell the medic what the patient touched, drank or breathed. Bring the container if you can do it safely.
## IF THEY ARE NOT WAKING UP Check that they are breathing. Turn them on their side. If you have been trained to use the purple bottle or a first aid autoinjector, use it. Then wait with them for the medic, and do not give anything else.
## IF YOU SEE SOMETHING YOU DO NOT UNDERSTAND Wounds that do not look like any tool did them. A patient who says something was on their face. A pain in the chest that came after. Do not try to treat it. Keep everyone back, tell the clinic exactly what you saw and tell the garrison too.
